gates.review_question: May the video use this Commons PD-self text-mode screenshot of Applesoft BASIC, credited as in evidence/rights.json, without further clearance?

claims.claim: The image shows the Applesoft BASIC prompt.
claims.where: Asset label; SCRIPT.md:73 'Your Apple II had Applesoft BASIC.'
claims.finding: Apple's manuals define ] as the Applesoft prompt (> is Integer BASIC, * is the Monitor). The image shows ] and runs HOME, INVERSE and NORMAL, which the Applesoft manual documents.

claims.claim: The image is an Apple II boot screen (ticket title; visual note at SCRIPT.md:75, 'Boot screens ... all showing their BASIC prompts').
claims.finding: The screen shows a program listing after RUN and LIST, not the power-on state. An Autostart ROM cold start shows a machine-name banner top centre (manual OCR reads 'APPLE II'); no banner is present. The asset is labelled as an Applesoft prompt, not a boot screen.
claims.review_question: Does the montage accept an Applesoft ] prompt screen (typed Hello World) for the Apple II tile, or does it need a true power-on screen? A true one needs a new capture; see the boundary need.

claims.claim: A specific Apple II model or ROM is shown.
claims.finding: Nothing on screen or on the file page identifies the model, ROM revision, or emulator. The raster is consistent with emulator output, but that is appearance, not evidence. No model name is used.

True of the Apple II Plus, which has Applesoft II in ROM in place of Integer BASIC. The original Apple II shipped with Integer BASIC in ROM, with Applesoft on cassette, disk, or a firmware card. By 1981 most Apples in use were II Plus machines. The sentence is defensible for the family in the early 1980s but not for every Apple II.
claims.review_question: Writing Lead (optional, low priority): keep 'Your Apple II had Applesoft BASIC', or tighten it to 'Your Apple II Plus had Applesoft BASIC'? Evidence supports either for a 1982 frame; no edit was made.
